what: Clicking a link to another page on the same site covers the screen with large accent-colored pixels. On a 256-high panel basis there are three layers of 32 · 16 · 8 cells, and each cell switches on at its own time (per layer .4 · .5 · all of the cells, start 0 to .48 + .16 × layer). Once progress passes that time, the cell steps through 4×4 Bayer thresholds over .2 and gets gradually denser. The curtain covers everything in 1.1s easeInOutQuad and navigates .22s later, and on the arriving page it lifts over the same length in a different cell order.

options.cover: Cover duration (seconds), default same as dur. At 0 it does not cover and switches immediately, only revealing the arriving page (for screens switched often, like apps)
options.hold: Time until moving on after fully covered (s), default .22
options.--fx-cover: Cover color (CSS variable — set on .fx-dither-cover in the user’s CSS), default var(--kf-accent)

use: <body data-fx="dither-cover" data-fx-dither-cover="cover: 0; dur: .4"> — Covers and uncovers when moving between pages that use the same part. Default is the original length

from.where: shared.js .dk-cover (yellow pixel curtain — loader and page transition) — original three layers of 32·16·8px · 4×4 dither · 1.1s easeInOutQuad · 220ms after covering

note: The cells belong to a 256-high panel, so they scale with screen height (112·56·28px on a 900px screen). The original also shows a loading indicator while covered on first open and then lifts it, but this part only lifts the arrival that was covered on leaving — the first loading curtain is left to the loader on the consuming side.
